    @pytest.mark.parametrize("children", [1, 2])
    def test_crossref_parent_inclusion_threshold(
        submission_command: tuple[str, ...], tmp_path: Path, children: int
    ) -> None:
        # btxdoc lines 163–175 and bibtex.web min_crossrefs=2: an uncited
        # parent is included only after two cited children refer to it. For a
        # single child, inheritance survives but its crossref pointer is removed.
        # Canonical parity corpora use explicit fields so this one rule cannot
        # mask eight independent style executions.
        bib = "".join(f'@misc{{c{i}, crossref = "p"}}\n' for i in range(children))
        bib += '@misc{p, year = "2020"}\n'
        style = r"""
    ENTRY { year } { } { }
    FUNCTION {emit}
    { cite$ write$ ":" write$
      crossref missing$ { "none" } { crossref } if$ write$
      ":" write$ year write$ newline$
    }
    READ
    ITERATE {emit}
    """
        bbl, _ = run_bibtex(
            submission_command, bib, style, [f"c{i}" for i in range(children)], tmp_path
        )
        expected = ["c0:none:2020"] if children == 1 else ["c0:p:2020", "c1:p:2020", "p:none:2020"]

review.editorial_summary: Completed the Python BibTeX implementation; unchanged source passes 374/386 under 1.2.4. Remaining gaps concern focused interpreter, declaration, crossref and name-selection behavior.
review.notes:
Official BibTeX 1.2.4 regrade: 375/386 under 1.2.3 becomes 374/386. The single changed observation is positive past-end format.name$ selection: the supplied WEB and 20 independent native-oracle probes retain the final scanned name, correcting the previous empty-result expectation. All 386 official outcome values match the frozen independently checked candidate; all 385 other node outcomes are exactly unchanged from 1.2.3. The changed score removes one false failure for Astra JavaScript and one false-credit point for each other submission; the correction follows supplied source authority and is applied consistently. No warning-kind, message, count or absence is imposed for the unmapped native diagnostic. Publicly permitted no-op top$, inter-token spaces, brace-width and quoted-unknown-warning choices remain accepted. All 8 canonical style integrations pass. Remaining failed observations are clustered below rather than presented as independent bug counts. Positive past-end name selection returns empty, whereas the supplied WEB retains the final scanned name. The corrected oracle removes former false credit; warning mapping remains unscored. Preamble values are joined with inserted spaces instead of direct concatenation. Commas after the second name comma are retained instead of discarded. One flush behavior retains trailing spaces and emits an all-space line. These two observations share an implementation cause; authoritative WEB output_bbl_line trims/discards them. Database MACRO names are wrongly exposed as executable BST functions instead of remaining in their distinct database namespace. Wrong-type concatenation coerces operands individually instead of producing the whole-operation empty-string default. A self-referential macro reuses its former binding instead of the source-defined self-reference behavior. The one-child/two-child boundary for including an uncited parent and retaining the crossref is implemented incorrectly. Dedicated controls localize this cause; the eight style integrations pass. Predefined crossref and sort.key$ redeclarations are accepted because predefined symbols are populated only after parsing. Two named assertions observe this declaration-order cause. Original full transcript/source reviews are retained below with exact path, hash, reviewer and payload; their prior tool-accounting claims are historical and superseded by the current session audit. Current session-based v2 tool count is 98 (originally recorded 97); proven corrections preserve the definition. Every input/output/cache/reasoning count and cost field is preserved; tokens remain complete and adapter reparse agrees. The original result bytes, generation metadata, source manifest and original score remain unchanged. Official audit source/hash, frozen test bytes and raw-score parsing all validate. Regrading makes no model calls and adds no generation cost. Run conditions: apps available but no external tool invocation observed.

Tool calls corrected from 97 to 98: proven rejected requests omitted from canonical items. Token totals, reasoning counts and generation cost are unchanged; original usage and session hashes are preserved in the regrade audit.

payload.summary: Completed a general BibTeX database parser and BST interpreter and exercised all four canonical styles. Unchanged Python source scores 375/386 against corrected BibTeX1.2.3; eleven focused interpreter/validation gaps remain, while all eight canonical style cases pass.
payload.notes: Completed voluntarily with a substantial standalone Python database parser and general BST interpreter, using the four supplied canonical styles rather than hard-coding their outputs. Full preserved transcript reviewed, including syntax compilation, all four styles, entry-type/field probes, arithmetic/string builtins, name formatting, citation/AUX behavior, crossref cycles, and structured malformed-input checks. Initial stack/type probe mistakes were corrected during iteration. No auth, quota, or disconnect interruption. Original 1.2.2 score was 353/376; saved unchanged source scores 375/386 against frozen independently reviewed 1.2.3 candidate. The candidate repairs illegal builtin redeclarations, undeclared style prerequisites, invalid crossref order/stack fixtures, unavailable Docker style paths, and incorrect reference-derived BBLs and micro-expectations. All eight independently regenerated canonical style cases now pass, while both focused crossref parent-threshold cases fail; this localizes the real threshold gap instead of penalizing eight styles for it. Eleven genuine remaining failures are: callable database MACROs (engine.py1306/1474 includes macro namespace among callable functions), wrong-type concatenation per-operand coercion (1567-1569), preamble separator insertion (1698), self-reference reusing the prior macro binding, one/two-child crossref threshold and retention (1185-1237), two builtin redeclarations allowed because predefined fields are added only after parsing (558-559), extra commas retained in First (799-801), and trailing/all-whitespace output retained by OutputBuffer. The documented always-space name formatting and ordinary-brace-zero width approximations remain accepted; they are not counted as model bugs. Independent compatible BibTeX oracle and supplied WEB establish the corrected expectations. Exact token/tool/reasoning usage reparse agrees with preserved session/events, requested gpt-5.6-terra/max; served identity remains null. Socket audit restricts allowed connections to chatgpt.com:443; full preserved session has exec_command/apply_patch only, no observed MCP, web-search or hosted-app calls. This run predates explicit hosted-app disablement and retains that cohort qualification. Original result/source/session/transcript and generation cost are unchanged; scratch regrading uses no new model calls. Awaiting official committed-suite regrade before publication.

payload.notes: Full transcript and source failure paths independently reviewed by audit_records. The committed suite reproduces 375/386; all eight independent-oracle style cases pass. Remaining failures concern database MACRO namespace, wrong-type concatenation, preamble concatenation, self-reference macro binding, the crossref threshold, predefined-field redeclaration, extra name commas and output whitespace. Crossref threshold failures are localized rather than amplified across style parity cases. Publicly permitted top$ no-op, name-spacing and brace-width approximations are accepted. Original 353/376 score and generated source remain intact. Tool accounting is corrected by a separate evidence audit.

evidence.reason: Explicit nested CreateProcess rejection, paired with one direct awaited request and absent from all canonical command items.

- Entry point: [output/main.py](/workspace/output/main.py)

It supports the requested flags, `.bib`/`.bst` execution, cites and `.aux` extraction, canonical styles, JSON logs/errors, and standard-library-only operation.

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("children", [1, 2])
    def test_crossref_parent_inclusion_threshold(
        submission_command: tuple[str, ...], tmp_path: Path, children: int
    ) -> None:
        # btxdoc lines 163–175 and bibtex.web min_crossrefs=2: an uncited
        # parent is included only after two cited children refer to it. For a
        # single child, inheritance survives but its crossref pointer is removed.
        # Canonical parity corpora use explicit fields so this one rule cannot
        # mask eight independent style executions.
        bib = "".join(f'@misc{{c{i}, crossref = "p"}}\n' for i in range(children))
        bib += '@misc{p, year = "2020"}\n'
        style = r"""
    ENTRY { year } { } { }
    FUNCTION {emit}
    { cite$ write$ ":" write$
      crossref missing$ { "none" } { crossref } if$ write$
      ":" write$ year write$ newline$
    }
    READ
    ITERATE {emit}
    """
        bbl, _ = run_bibtex(
            submission_command, bib, style, [f"c{i}" for i in range(children)], tmp_path
        )
        expected = ["c0:none:2020"] if children == 1 else ["c0:p:2020", "c1:p:2020", "p:none:2020"]
>       assert bbl.splitlines() == expected
E       AssertionError: assert ['c0:p:2020'] == ['c0:none:2020']
